newsitem.title: USA: Private NY class-action suit launched vs tobacco.
newsitem.headline: Private NY class-action suit launched vs tobacco.

text.p: Two New York law firms headed by former New York state Supreme Court justices joined forces in a suit seeking class action status against the tobacco industry specifying lung and throat cancer victims as the suit's plaintiff base.

The suit was filed April 30 by Finz & Finz P.C.and Stanley R. Waxman P.C on behalf of four named plaintiffs, one of whom is already dead, and which seeks class status on behalf of all New York state residents seeks unspecified compensatory and punitive damages from the entire industry, including its advertising, manufacturing and research arms.

The new suit - the latest in a seemingly endless barrage of litigation against the industry - comes one day after a Florida jury found R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, not liable for the 1995 death of a former smoker.
Undaunted by Monday's decision, the plaintiffs' attorneys said their suit is distinct from other mass and individual litigation efforts currently facing the industry.
It targets throat and lung cancer as the specific injury, while most other suits have been general and had no specification of injury.
In a previous attempt at a national class-action suit, the so-called Castano suit, the injury specified was addiction.
Other class actions have specified consumer fraud or deception or other aspects of the industry's alleged offenses.

The national class status of Castano was overturned May 23, 1996. The consortium of 60 law firms that filed the suit has begun to refile the suit, again seeking class status, on a state-by-state basis.

The suit alleges a concerted action among all players in the industry to commit a "wrongful conspiracy" designed to "conceal and misrepresent information about cigarettes, particularly the carcinogenic properties of tar, and the highly addictive nature of nicotine, all leading to...tragic deaths."

Besides the Castano derivative suits, there are several other class-action suits that have been brought by private law firms, and there are 25 class-action suits that have been brought by as many state attorneys general.
The state attorneys suits have also targeted the entire industry and seek reimbursement for billions of dollars in state Medicaid funds used to treat smoking-related sicknesses.

"Our case is not related to Castano. That litigation addresses the addiction issue and not the individual injuries of cancer victims by their health conditions," said Stuart Finz, of Finz & Finz P.C., one of the two firms that brought the suit.
Finz is the son and colleague of Leonard Finz, who served as a New York State Supreme Court justice for 13 years.

The other legal firm behind the suit is Stanley R. Waxman P.C., with General Counsel Joseph Kunzeman. Kunzeman also spent 13 years on the state Supreme Court and seven years in the state's Appellate Court division.
"We will bring the entire industry into one courtroom so that one jury can see the conspiracy unfold," Leonard Finz said.
